content.title: Why Iowa basketball's Ben McCollum is top newcomer coach in Big Ten
content.text: March 18, 2026, 6:01 a.m. CTIOWA CITY — After the end of the regular season, the Big Ten handed out a list of individual honors. All-conference teams, Coach of the Year, Player of the Year, Freshman of the Year and other recognition of that nature.The Big Ten doesn’t have an award for Big Ten Newcomer Coach of the Year. But if it did, Iowa's Ben McCollum would very likely be the recipient.Four Big Ten programs had new head coaches this season — Iowa, Indiana, Maryland and Minnesota. The Hawkeyes are the only one of that group to make the 2026 NCAA Tournament.There have been some obvious growing pains for Iowa this season. McCollum knows there was meat left on the bone, as he pointed out after the Hawkeyes’ NCAA Tournament matchup with Clemson was announced, saying, “You win half those close games and you’re looking at three to four more wins.”But with so much to sort out after being hired, it’s not easy to make the NCAA Tournament in your first season at the helm, especially in the grinder of the Big Ten. Just look at the other three schools that were in a similar position this season.Iowa (21-12 overall, 10-10 Big Ten)Indiana (18-14, 9-11)Minnesota (15-17, 8-12)Maryland (12-21, 4-16)If you want even more context, look at last season.There were four Big Ten programs with new head coaches last season — Michigan, USC, Ohio State and Washington — that’s counting the Buckeyes’ Jake Diebler, who had previously served in an interim role, but was in his first season in the permanent position.Nevertheless, only one of those four programs made the NCAA Tournament last season: Michigan. That means, in the last two seasons, Big Ten coaches in their first season at the helm have gone just 2-for-8 in making the NCAA Tournament. The two to do so are Michigan’s Dusty May and Iowa’s Ben McCollum.Some Big Ten coaches who have been with their schools for more than one year still haven’t broken through. Danny Sprinkle is 0-for-2 at Washington. Eric Musselman is 0-for-2 at USC. Mike Rhoades is 0-for-3 at Penn State.So what has allowed Iowa to be ahead of the curve?“I think the personnel,” McCollum said. “We really honed in on people and made sure we got the right people for the most part — as players and then as a staff. We focused so much on that and I think that’s helped us from a character perspective, helped us get off the ground early.”The fact that McCollum brought so many players and staff members to Iowa from Drake became both a point of skepticism and a reason for optimism. On the one hand, it looked like McCollum was attempting to make a mid-major program translate to the Big Ten level. On the other hand, Iowa wasn't starting over from scratch.The only player Darian DeVries brought with him from West Virginia to Indiana was his son, Tucker — DeVries also previously coached Conor Enright at Drake — but there was not the level of continuity that Iowa had. That was similar to Niko Medved at Minnesota, who brought Jaylen Crocker-Johnson with him from Colorado State, but had mostly a new group."What coach McCollum has done, bringing a lot of us in and building that culture and having retention," Cam Manyawu explained, "it made it that much easier to bring other guys along. So the chemistry built really, really fast and I think we kind of had a jumpstart on other teams.”Maryland’s roster was built closer to Iowa’s in the sense that Buzz Williams brought four former Texas A&M players with him to College Park. But the Terrapins were bitten by injuries, including to Pharrel Payne, an All-Big Ten-caliber big man who appeared in only 10 games this season.That reveals an underrated part of Iowa’s success this season: the ability to stay healthy. Outside of an injury to Peyton McCollum and an illness to Trey Thompson, McCollum had almost the entire roster at his disposal over the course of the season.Look at the difference in the Big Ten availability report when Iowa played Maryland in the Big Ten Tournament.Iowa player out: Peyton McCollum.Maryland players out: Myles Rice, Pharrel Payne, Rakease Passmore and Lukas Sotell.It was rough in that department for Minnesota, too. The Golden Gophers could’ve made more noise this season, but were handicapped by a roster decimated by injuries.Minnesota players out vs. Rutgers in the Big Ten Tournament included: Chansey Willis Jr., Jaylen Crocker-Johnson, Chance Stephens, BJ Omot and Robert Vaihola.Iowa avoided a brutal injury situation like that.And then, there is what you could consider The McCollum Effect.Part of what generated so much excitement upon McCollum’s hiring was his track record as a winner — the four Division II national titles, and a 31-4 record in his only season at Drake. It is possible that McCollum’s coaching has been a difference-maker as to why Iowa is the only Big Ten program to make the NCAA Tournament this season with a new head coach.“Coach (McCollum) and the coaching staff,” star senior Bennett Stirtz said. “ He’s a great coach, obviously. Super young coach. But he’s one of the best in the country. He just recruits the right guys. It’s a special group.”Having Stirtz, one of the best players in the Big Ten, made it easier for Iowa to accomplish that, too. Plus, the Hawkeyes were able to overcome their roster deficiencies better than a team like Indiana.Of course, this season is not the end-all, be-all for these new coaches. They will be judged on the entirety of their tenure, not just the first season, so it’s important to let things play out.The marathon is more important than the sprint.But so far, Iowa has won the sprint.Follow Tyler Tachman on X @Tyler_T15, contact via email at ttachman@gannett.com
